relationships.subject: Varicella-zoster virus
relationships.evidence_quote: we confirmed that VZV infection could significantly upregulate the expression of T-type calcium channel Cav3.2 in DRG and spinal dorsal horn (SDH)

relationships.subject: (2R/S)-6-prenylnaringenin
relationships.evidence_quote: Intrathecal administration of Cav3.2 blocker (2R/S)-6-prenylnaringenin (6-PNG) relieved mechanical and thermal hyperalgesia induced by VZV.

relationships.subject: Cav3.2
relationships.evidence_quote: Cav3.2 played a key role in zoster-associated pain and had the potential to be a novel drug target

key_findings: VZV infection upregulates Cav3.2 (not Cav3.1/3.3) in mouse DRG and spinal dorsal horn, in parallel with mechanical and thermal allodynia.
Intrathecal Cav3.2 blocker 6-PNG relieved VZV-induced hyperalgesia.
